---
title: "Data catalog"
---

The datasets that the `oceanbench` library uses are described in the [OceanBench data catalog on EDITO](https://datalab.dive.edito.eu/data-catalog/data/catalogs/projects/oceanbench/oceanbench-catalog), that you can browse online.
It follows the [STAC](https://stacspec.org) specification.

For each dataset, the catalog tells you what it contains and how to open it.

## Collections

Challengers

:   Forecasts of the evaluated ocean forecasting systems, and baselines.

References

:   Analyses, reanalyses, observations and static fields that challengers are compared against.

Inputs

:   Initial states and forcings that challengers use to produce their forecasts, see [input datasets](/documentation/input-datasets-for-oceanbench-challenger-evaluation/index.qmd).

Training

:   Datasets to train ocean forecasting systems on, without overlapping the evaluation period.

## Datasets

Each dataset is described by a STAC item with:

- its spatial and temporal extent, dimensions and variables (with CF standard names and units),
- Python examples to open it, with the [`oceanbench` datasets API](/documentation/api/index.qmd) or the Copernicus Marine Toolbox,
- the `oceanbench:library_usage` property, telling whether the `oceanbench` library uses it.

## Programmatic access

The catalog is also served by the EDITO STAC API at `https://api.dive.edito.eu/data/catalogs/projects/oceanbench/oceanbench-catalog`, for example with [`pystac`](https://pystac.readthedocs.io):

```python
import pystac

catalog = pystac.Catalog.from_file(
    "https://api.dive.edito.eu/data/catalogs/projects/oceanbench/oceanbench-catalog"
)
for collection in catalog.get_children():
    print(collection.id, collection.title)
```
